cls: Antiflatulent / antifoaming agent (inert silicone polymer surfactant)
pharm: An inert, non-absorbed silicone polymer (dimeticone/polydimethylsiloxane; activated form = simeticone) that lowers the surface tension of gas bubbles in the gut so they coalesce and are more easily expelled. Physiologically inert and not systemically absorbed; not FDA-approved as a drug (sold OTC).
quick: ~40-250 mg per dose after meals and at bedtime (region-dependent); EU 100-250 mg, US 40-125 mg (max ~500 mg/day)
Usually taken after meals and at bedtime
None required; review if adult symptoms persist beyond ~2 weeks
summary: Methylpolysiloxane refers to the silicone antifoaming agents dimeticone (polydimethylsiloxane) and its activated form simeticone (dimeticone plus finely divided silica). It is an antiflatulent that physically lowers the surface tension of gas bubbles in the gastrointestinal tract, causing small bubbles to coalesce so that trapped gas is more easily passed by belching or flatus; it does NOT reduce gas production. It is pharmacologically and physiologically inert, is not systemically absorbed, and is excreted unchanged in feces. It is used for flatulence, bloating, functional dyspepsia, aerophagia, infant colic (efficacy unproven), and as a defoaming aid before endoscopy/colonoscopy or abdominal imaging. Because it is not absorbed it is exceptionally safe, including in pregnancy, lactation, renal/hepatic impairment, and infants, and requires no monitoring. It is sold OTC and is not FDA-approved as a drug. NOTE: This record draws on BNF/NHS, EMA-style SmPC, and Martindale references; adult per-dose figures differ by region (EU 100-250 mg vs US 40-125 mg).
indications: Flatulence, bloating, and abdominal distension due to excess gastrointestinal gas
Functional dyspepsia / functional bloating and aerophagia
Infant colic / trapped wind (efficacy unproven, but widely used)
Defoaming aid before/during endoscopy, colonoscopy, and abdominal radiography/ultrasound to improve mucosal visualization

dosage.t: After meals and at bedtime (up to 3-4 times daily)
Four times daily after meals and at bedtime
Four times daily (after meals and bedtime)

dosage.d: 20 mg per dose (e.g., one dropperful = 0.5 mL of 40 mg/mL)
dosage.t: Up to several times daily / before feeds
dosage.n: Maximum about 240 mg/day; follow the specific product

dosage.t: About 20 min to 1 hour before the procedure

admin: Take after meals and at bedtime for symptomatic gas relief
Chew chewable tablets fully before swallowing; swallow capsules/tablets whole with water
Measure liquids and infant drops with the supplied syringe/dropper, not a kitchen spoon
For infants, drops may be mixed into milk or feed; give before feeds where the product directs
Often co-formulated with antacids, loperamide, or charcoal
moa: Methylpolysiloxane (dimeticone/simeticone) is a surfactant that decreases the surface tension of gas bubbles within the gastrointestinal lumen. This causes small entrapped gas bubbles and mucus-coated foam to coalesce into larger bubbles that are more easily eliminated by belching or as flatus (or absorbed through the gut wall). It does not reduce or prevent the formation of gas - it only disperses existing foam. Simeticone (activated dimeticone) contains added silicon dioxide that enhances this antifoaming action. The agent is physiologically inert and is not systemically absorbed.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to simeticone/dimeticone or any excipient
relative: Not indicated for bowel obstruction or ileus (will not relieve these)
monitor: Adult symptoms persisting beyond ~2 weeks of regular use should prompt medical review

preg: Considered safe in pregnancy because it is not systemically absorbed; well tolerated. (Some legacy US labels carried a formal pregnancy category, but the lack of absorption underpins its safety.)
lact: Considered safe during breastfeeding; not systemically absorbed.
renal: No dose adjustment is required - the agent is not absorbed and is excreted unchanged in feces.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required - the agent is not absorbed and is excreted unchanged in feces.

minor: Theoretically may slightly reduce absorption of some co-administered oral drugs; isolated reports with levothyroxine (separate by ~4 hours) and carbamazepine
interactions.food: Usually taken after meals; no significant food interaction.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference; not measurable in serum (non-absorbed).

rare: Mild nausea, constipation, or loose stools

monitoring: Review or seek medical advice if adult symptoms persist beyond about 14 days of regular use
counsel: This medicine disperses gas bubbles to ease bloating and wind, but it does not stop gas from forming
It is very safe and can be used in infants and during pregnancy
Chew chewable tablets fully; measure liquids with the device provided
For babies, it may take a few days of regular use; a missed dose is harmless
See a clinician if adult symptoms last more than about 2 weeks or get worse
pk: Acts locally in the gut; symptomatic relief is usually rapid
Acts as gas bubbles are encountered; taken as needed/after meals
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture (per product label)
pearls: Physiologically inert and not absorbed - exceptionally safe, including pregnancy, lactation, renal/hepatic impairment, and infants
Disperses gas bubbles; does NOT reduce gas production
Simeticone = activated dimeticone (dimeticone plus silica) and is the more effective antifoam
Evidence for infant colic is weak (no clear benefit over placebo) despite heavy OTC use
Increasingly used as a pre-endoscopy/colonoscopy defoaming aid to improve mucosal visualization
Sold OTC; NOT FDA-approved as a drug. Adult dosing differs by region (EU 100-250 mg vs US 40-125 mg, max ~500 mg/day)
missed: This medicine is taken as needed, so a missed dose is not a problem. Take it when you remember, or skip it if it is nearly time for the next dose; do not double up.
overdose: Overdose is not toxic given the lack of absorption; at most it may cause mild gastrointestinal upset (loose stools or constipation). No specific treatment is required beyond stopping the product.
